case_name: Raghavendra Sharma v State Of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State Of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

7 November 2008
Criminal Appeal No. 1063 of 2001
The Judgment was delivered by: Dr. Arijit Pasayat, J.
1. Challenge in this appeal is to the judgement of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, Jabalpur upholding the conviction of the appellant for offence punishable u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the ' IPC ') as was recorded by learned Second Additional Sessions Judge, Chhindwara in Sessions Trial No. 136 of 1986. Appellant alongwith his father Bhuvneshwar Dayal Sharma faced trial for commission of offences punishable u/s. 302 read with S. 34 and 201 IPC. Father of  the appellant was acquitted of both the charges, while appellant was acquitted of charges u/s. 201.
2. Background facts in a nutshell are as follows: Maya (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased') was the wife of the appellant and they were married about 11 months prior to the date of incident. It is further an admitted position that the decea
facts: Maya was the wife of the appellant, and they were married about 11 months prior to the date of incident.
The deceased was a teacher posted at Parasia, while the appellant was also a teacher posted at village Mungwani.
The couple had gone to Vidisha along with Rajkumari (P.W.10) and her husband Radhakrishan and Dipak.
They stayed there for about ten days and thereafter on 19.5.1988, the appellant along with the deceased and Dipak returned to village Parasia.
The deceased was at an advanced stage of pregnancy and died in the night between 21-22 May, 1986 at her father-in-law's place at village Salkhani.
On receipt of the information about the death of Maya, Mahesh Prasad (P.W.1) went to village Salkhani with Sushila (P.W.8) and Narendra Kumar Sharma (P.W.2).
They perceived her death to be suspicious and gave a report to the Chourai Police Station.
The investigating agency also sent the earth containing vomited material for chemical examination to the Forensic Science Laboratory.
issues: Whether the death of Maya was homicidal or accidental in nature?
petitioner_arguments: Appellant's stand that the death of Maya was accidental in nature.
Appellant's argument that he had motive to commit the crime due to his wife's alleged illicit relationship with her brother-in-law Radhakrishan.
respondent_arguments: State's argument that the conclusions of the trial court were justified and the death of Maya was homicidal in nature.
State's support for the judgment of the High Court.
court_reasoning: The trial court found that the appellant doubted the fidelity of his wife and believed that she had illicit relationship with her brother-in-law and was not happy with the dowry articles given to him at the time of marriage.
The trial court rejected the evidence of Dr. S.D. Vaidya, DW3 who had opined that the death of Maya was accidental in nature.
The High Court analyzed the stand taken by the appellant and came to hold that the conclusions of the trial court were justified.
